The part of an item, and the size of a part

Source: R/structured.R
part_of.Rd

For a partition P from part_var(), part_of(item, P) is the part an item is in, and size_of(part, P) is how many items a part holds. For people divided into teams, part_of(3, teams) is the team of person 3, and size_of(1, teams) is the number of people in team 1.

Usage

part_of(item, P)

size_of(part, P)

Arguments

item

Items: whole numbers from 1 to the number of items.

P

A partition from part_var().

part

Parts: whole numbers from 1 to the number of parts.

Value

An expression with one element per element of the first argument: for part_of() each a whole number from 1 to the number of parts, for size_of() each a whole number from 0 to the number of items.

Details

The result is an expression whose value the service chooses, like the value of a decision variable. To read data that depends on an item's part, index a lookup_table() with part_of().

The first argument is a plain number, or a vector of numbers, and both functions return one element per number: part_of(1:5, P) is the parts of the first five items, an expression of length 5.

Examples

m <- model()
teams <- part_var(m, "teams", 5, 2)
part_of(3, teams)                   # the team of person 3
#> part_of(3, teams)
size_of(1, teams)                   # how many people are in team 1
#> size_of(1, teams)
part_of(1:5, teams)                 # everyone's team
#> [1] part_of(1, teams)
#> [2] part_of(2, teams)
#> [3] part_of(3, teams)
#> [4] part_of(4, teams)
#> [5] part_of(5, teams)
